topic: Fundamental Constants and Mathematical Structure in Turbulence

sections.title: Introduction: The Chaos in the Fluid
lecture_lines: Turbulence is an energy cascade of chaotic fluid motion.
Inertial forces dominate at high velocities.
Viscous forces eventually dampen the flow motion.
animations: Show cascade of chaotic vectors in #3498DB color.
Animate inertial force vectors pushing fluid outward in #E74C3C color.
Show viscous dampening as fluid particles slowly fading in #2ECC71 color.

sections.title: The Kolmogorov Hypotheses (1941)
lecture_lines: Energy cascades from large scales to small.
Small-scale turbulence is isotropic and universal.
Governed by dissipation rate and viscosity.
animations: Show large eddies breaking down into smaller vortices in #3498DB color.
Show small-scale vortices behaving uniformly in all directions.
Animate labels ε (energy dissipation) and ν (kinematic viscosity) in #F1C40F color.

sections.title: Mathematical Structure: The Energy Spectrum
lecture_lines: Wavenumber k relates to eddy scale size.
The spectrum shows power density versus wavenumber.
Energy cascades down across these scales.
This structure reveals underlying mathematical order.
animations: Display E(k) proportional to k^-5/3 formula in #F1C40F color.
Display wavenumber k on a horizontal axis moving right.
Show the energy spectrum plot shifting as k increases.
Animate energy flowing across k-scales represented by moving particles.
Display order emerging from chaos as a structured grid in #2ECC71 color.

sections.title: The Kolmogorov Length Scale (η)
lecture_lines: Viscosity turns kinetic energy into heat.
Eta is the smallest turbulence length scale.
Formula: η equals ν cubed over ε.
animations: Show viscous heating converting energy to heat in #E74C3C color.
Display the smallest length scale η as a glowing point in #3498DB.
Display η = (ν³/ε)^(1/4) formula and highlight it in #F1C40F.

sections.title: Summary and Real-world Application
lecture_lines: Energy enters large and dissipates at η.
Constants enable modeling without tracking atoms.
Turbulence models help design efficient systems.
animations: Show the full range from large input to η dissipation.
Show a modeling framework icon representing the cascade in #3498DB.
Animate a falcon soaring, highlighting turbulence-informed wing design in #2ECC71.
